channel.title: Cadence Evidence — PT Research Signal
channel.description: Daily curated physical therapy & rehab research for clinicians. AI-scored signal from 56 sources.

item.title: Biological effects of technique-specific manual therapy in healthy individuals and people with musculoskeletal disorders: a systematic review with meta-analysis.
item.description: This systematic review with meta-analysis evaluates the neurophysiological and metabolic effects of technique-specific manual therapy (HVLA vs. non-HVLA) in healthy individuals and people with musculoskeletal disorders, registered prospectively in PROSPERO.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: [Articles] Liposuction versus conservative therapy for patients with lipoedema in Germany: a multicentre, randomised controlled clinical trial
item.description: A multicenter, randomized controlled clinical trial in Germany found liposuction to be superior to conservative therapy in reducing leg pain and improving quality of life for patients with lipoedema, despite being associated with a higher rate of serious adverse events.
item.author: The Lancet

item.title: Physiotherapist-led care for musculoskeletal conditions in the emergency department (RESHAP-ED): a randomised controlled trial with economic evaluation.
item.description: The RESHAP-ED randomized controlled trial found that physiotherapist-led care for musculoskeletal conditions in the emergency department significantly reduced length of stay and healthcare costs while maintaining non-inferior safety compared to usual care.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Paired comparison of extrinsic feedback effects on motor learning and functional recovery after stroke: a secondary analysis of randomized controlled trials.
item.description: A secondary analysis of randomized controlled trials (updated through November 2025) compared the effects of extrinsic feedback on motor learning versus functional recovery after stroke, calculating standardized mean differences using random-effects meta-analysis and accounting for within-study dependence.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Digital therapeutic combining exercise and cognitive-behavioural therapy reduces pain in patients with chronic patellofemoral pain: a multicentre randomised controlled trial.
item.description: An 8-week smartphone-based multidisciplinary digital therapeutic combining exercise and cognitive-behavioural therapy significantly reduced usual knee pain in 216 participants with chronic patellofemoral pain compared to education and exercise instruction.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Focal Muscle Vibration for Upper Limb Spasticity After Stroke: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis found that focal muscle vibration (FMV) can improve upper limb spasticity after stroke, with effects potentially moderated by frequency, amplitude, or target joint.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Sensorimotor effects of heatwrap and exercise in acute low back pain: results of a randomised controlled trial
item.description: A randomized controlled trial (N=99) found that heatwrap combined with exercise was more effective than sham heatwrap in improving pain sensitivity, lumbar muscle activity, current pain intensity, and trunk flexion range of motion in acute low back pain.
item.author: medRxiv

item.title: Tailoring Resistance Exercise for Knee Osteoarthritis: An Intervention Systematic Review With Dose-Response Meta-analysis of the Effects of Intensity and Volume.
item.description: A systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis of RCTs found dose-response relationships between isotonic lower extremity resistance exercise volume and outcomes of pain, function, and strength in people with knee osteoarthritis (OA), and compared different intensities and delivery methods.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: The Efficacy of Exercise Therapy for Nonspecific Chronic Low Back Pain According to the FITT Principle: A Systematic Review With Meta-analyses.
item.description: A systematic review with meta-analyses evaluated the efficacy of exercise therapy interventions, differing in frequency, intensity, type, and time (FITT), on disability in individuals with nonspecific chronic low back pain (LBP).
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Biofeedback in Parkinson's disease: A systematic review with meta-analysis.
item.description: A systematic review with meta-analysis found that biofeedback added to practice significantly improves lower limb activity in individuals with Parkinson's disease compared to practice alone.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Gait Speed Changes in Stroke Rehabilitation Motor Lower Extremity Randomized Controlled Trials by Intervention and Time Post-Stroke: A Meta-Analysis
item.description: A meta-analysis examined gait speed changes in randomized controlled trials of motor lower extremity stroke rehabilitation across various interventions, compared to conventional care or sham controls, at different time points post-stroke.
item.author: Archives of PM&R

item.title: Comparison of high-intensity laser therapy and extracorporeal shock wave therapy for the treatment of plantar flexor spasticity in post-stroke patients.
item.description: This prospective, randomized, controlled, parallel-group clinical trial with 42 stroke patients compared high-intensity laser therapy and extracorporeal shock wave therapy, each combined with rehabilitation, versus rehabilitation alone, for treating plantar flexor spasticity.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Home-based digital exercise versus hospital physiotherapy for plantar fasciitis: a propensity-score-matched retrospective cohort study with dual-perspective cost-utility evaluation.
item.description: A propensity-score-matched retrospective cohort study in China found that a 12-week home-based digital exercise program was non-inferior to hospital-supervised physiotherapy for plantar fasciitis regarding first-step morning pain (adjusted mean difference -0.63 points, 95% CI -0.92 to -0.35; p < 0.001) and showed cost-utility advantages from both payer and societal perspectives.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: The effectiveness of instrument-assisted soft tissue mobilization on pain and function in patients with musculoskeletal disorders: a systematic review and meta-analysis
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 14 RCTs (n=550) found that instrument-assisted soft tissue mobilization (IASTM) significantly improved pain (SMD -0.74; 95% CI -1.04 to -0.44) and function (SMD -0.66; 95% CI -0.99 to -0.34) in musculoskeletal disorders in the short term, with moderate effect sizes.
item.author: BMC Musculoskelet Disord

item.title: Reframing patient expectations as therapeutic targets in musculoskeletal care.
item.description: Patient expectations (PEs) are often underappreciated but profoundly impactful in musculoskeletal pain management. This professional practice article argues that PEs are modifiable therapeutic targets, extending beyond treatment and recovery to encompass relational, contextual, lifestyle, spiritual, and cultural dimensions.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Impact of Social Determinants of Health on Physical Therapy Utilization in Home Health and Outpatient Settings: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
item.description: This cross-sectional study of Medicare fee-for-service claims identified patient-, hospital-, and regional-level social determinants of health (SDOH) factors associated with home health and outpatient physical therapy utilization after lower extremity joint replacement.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Developing biopsychosocial competence in musculoskeletal pain care: Australian physiotherapy educators' perspectives.
item.description: This qualitative study explores the perspectives of 18 Australian physiotherapy educators on translating the biopsychosocial approach to pain care from knowing to doing, identifying challenges in practical clinical adoption.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: The Impact of Upper Extremity Rehabilitation on Fatigue in Individuals With Multiple Sclerosis: A Systematic Review.
item.description: This systematic review evaluates and synthesizes existing evidence on the effects of upper extremity rehabilitation interventions on fatigue in individuals with multiple sclerosis, following PRISMA guidelines and PROSPERO registration.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: The Effect of Robot-Assisted Gait Training on Balance, Gait and Kinesiophobia in Individuals With Post-Stroke Hemiparesis: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
item.description: This single-blind, parallel-group randomized controlled trial with 60 participants explored the effects of adding robot-assisted gait training to conventional rehabilitation on balance, gait, and kinesiophobia in individuals with post-stroke hemiparesis.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Comparison of action observation therapy and virtual reality combined with conventional therapy for upper extremity rehabilitation in children with unilateral cerebral palsy.
item.description: This study randomized 45 children (aged 5-15 years) with unilateral cerebral palsy into three groups (AOT, XBOX Kinect, Conventional) to compare the effects of action observation therapy and virtual reality combined with conventional therapy on upper extremity function.
item.author: PubMed
